surviving.title: Core's unlayered CSS removes the Input focus ring and invalid ring in every consuming product
surviving.evidence: packages/core/src/styles.css: `.framework-scope [data-slot="button"], .framework-scope [data-slot="card"], .framework-scope [data-slot="input"] { box-shadow: var(--brand-shadow); }` sits outside any @layer, so under Tailwind v4 it beats every layered utility regardless of specificity. input.tsx:11-12 draws the focus and error states as box-shadow (`focus-visible:ring-[3px] focus-visible:ring-ring`, `aria-invalid:ring-destructive/20`). Measured with Playwright on /forms?brand=neutral and ?brand=rapold, #form-title with :focus-visible true: outline 'none', box-shadow 'none' (--brand-shadow resolves to 'none'). The only remaining focus cue is a 1px border-colour change. The same unlayered file sets `[data-size=default]{padding:10px 20px;font-size:1rem}`, so a consumer's `<Button className="px-3">` is ignored (measured padding 10px 20px).
surviving.principle: WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA). WCAG 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (AAA) as the target. CSS cascade layers: brand overrides must not outrank component utilities.
surviving.fix: Put every styles.css rule after @theme inside `@layer base` or `@layer components`, and use `:where(.framework-scope) [data-slot=…]` so specificity stays 0. Feed the brand shadow into the cva class (e.g. `shadow-[var(--brand-shadow)]`) and compose it with the ring: `focus-visible:shadow-[0_0_0_3px_var(--ring),var(--brand-shadow)]`. Do the same for the button min-height and padding (use cva size tokens such as `h-[var(--brand-button-height)] px-5`). Add a Playwright assertion that the focused Input has a non-'none' box-shadow or outline.
surviving.harm_chain: A product team uses the Atlas Input in Auth, Lotse or another product. Keyboard users see only a hairline colour shift on focus, and invalid fields lose their red ring, so the state is signalled by border colour alone. Every product inherits this.
surviving.anticipated_refutation: The border still changes colour, so 2.4.7 is technically met. That holds only if the 1px border reaches 3:1 against its unfocused colour. The component author clearly intended a 3px ring, and the cascade silently removes it.
surviving.vreason: Confirmed in packages/core/src/styles.css:49-50: the box-shadow and button padding rules sit outside the @layer base block that closes at line 48. They are unlayered, so they beat Tailwind v4's layered ring utilities from input.tsx:11-12. Focus and invalid now rely only on a border-colour change. 2.4.7 may technically pass on the border alone, but the 3px ring the author intended is silently removed in every consuming product, so P1 stands. No doc justifies this. I did not re-run the Playwright measurement; the cascade analysis is enough.

surviving.title: Brand-shadow override deletes the focus ring on Button and Input; keyboard focus is near-invisible
surviving.evidence:
packages/core/src/styles.css:49 `.framework-scope [data-slot="button"], ... [data-slot="input"] { box-shadow: var(--brand-shadow); }` is unlayered, so it beats the Tailwind utility `focus-visible:ring-[3px] focus-visible:ring-ring` in button.tsx:8 and input.tsx:12.

Measured live on /components?brand=rapold, light mode, keyboard Tab:
- Primäraktion: box-shadow 'none', outline 'solid 3px rgb(255,255,255)' at offset 0. White on page bg #F4FAFF is 1.05:1.
- Input #demo-project: box-shadow 'none', outline 'none'. The only cue is a 1px border change from --input #6F87A0 to --ring #0066B3, which is 1.59:1 between the two states.
- The same happens in all 6 brand-modes (inputFocus.shadow 'none', or the brand shadow '0 1px 3px #00000014' on dominicano).
- The docs rule in globals.css `a:focus-visible,button:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--ring);outline-offset:3px}` does not produce a ring-colored outline on Buttons (computed color = currentColor, offset 0).

Screenshots: focus-primary.png and focus-input.png in the scratchpad.
surviving.principle: WCAG 2.2 SC 2.4.7 Focus Visible (risk), SC 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (fails: 3px area at >=3:1 change), SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast; Nielsen #1 visibility of system status
surviving.fix:
Move styles.css:49-52 into `@layer components` so utilities win. Also define one focus token and compose it with the brand shadow:
`--focus-ring: 0 0 0 var(--border-width-focus) var(--ring)` and `[data-slot=button]:focus-visible{box-shadow:var(--brand-shadow),var(--focus-ring)}`.
Add a Playwright assertion that every focusable primitive shows a >=3:1 indicator change in all 6 brand-modes.
surviving.harm_chain: Primitive ships with ring utility, brand CSS silently overrides it, every Rapold product consuming core inherits invisible focus on its primary CTA and inputs, keyboard users lose their place
surviving.anticipated_refutation: The input border still changes color. But a 1px hue shift at 1.59:1 does not meet focus-appearance guidance, and the primary button gets no visible change at all.
surviving.vreason: Confirmed in source: packages/core/src/styles.css:49 is an unlayered rule `.framework-scope [data-slot="button"], ... [data-slot="input"] { box-shadow: var(--brand-shadow); }`. Tailwind v4 utilities sit in @layer utilities, and unlayered CSS always beats layered CSS, so the `focus-visible:ring-[3px] focus-visible:ring-ring` box-shadow in button.tsx:8 and input.tsx:12 never applies. The same rule also kills the `aria-invalid:ring-destructive/20` shadow. The measured result is plausible: a currentColor (white) outline at offset 0 on the primary button, and only a 1px border change on the input. Nothing in README, AGENTS.md or docs/apple-design-audit.md treats this as intended; audit row A03 even lists the visual focus check as still open. It hits the primary CTA and inputs of every product that consumes core, so P1 holds (WCAG 2.4.7 risk, 2.4.13/1.4.11). The fix is sound: put the rule in @layer components, or compose brand-shadow with a focus ring.

surviving.title: Core Button and Input focus ring is wiped out by an unlayered brand-shadow rule. Products using @rapold/framework-core get no visible focus on Button.
surviving.evidence:
packages/core/src/styles.css:49 sets `.framework-scope [data-slot="button"], ... [data-slot="input"] { box-shadow: var(--brand-shadow); }` outside any @layer, so it beats Tailwind's layered `focus-visible:ring-[3px] focus-visible:ring-ring` (button.tsx:8, input.tsx:12). Button also sets `outline-none`.

Measured on /components with the 'Primäraktion' button focused by keyboard: box-shadow 'none'. Its only indicator is the docs-only rule in globals.css:21 (`button:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--ring)}`). With that docs rule neutralised to simulate a consumer app: outline none, border 0px, box-shadow none, so there is no indicator at all.

Input #demo-project focused by keyboard: box-shadow none and outline none. The only change is the 1px border going from --input #737b88 to --ring #263b70, about a 2.5:1 change (screenshot taken). In forced-colors mode, the focused input border is rgb(55,0,110) against rgb(0,0,0) unfocused, which is effectively invisible.
surviving.principle: WCAG 2.4.7 Focus Visible (AA) and 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast (AA) for focus indicators; see also 2.4.13 Focus Appearance (AAA). For a design system the failure carries into every consumer product (AI Fabric, Argus, Cockpit, …).
surviving.fix: Move line 49 into `@layer components`, or scope it to `:not(:focus-visible)`. Better still, make core focus outline-based so it survives forced colors: add `focus-visible:outline-2 focus-visible:outline-offset-2 focus-visible:outline-ring` to the buttonVariants base and Input, replacing `outline-none`. Add a regression test that renders Button and Input without the docs globals.css and checks that the computed outline or box-shadow is not 'none' when focus-visible.
surviving.harm_chain: A consumer app imports core styles.css but not the Atlas docs globals.css → keyboard focus on Button disappears → a keyboard or switch user cannot tell which action they are about to trigger. That is an AA failure in every Rapold product, and it stays hidden because the reference site masks it.
surviving.anticipated_refutation: 'Atlas itself shows a 3px outline.' It does, but only because of apps/docs/app/globals.css:21. The core package is the deliverable, and its own focus ring is dead code.
surviving.vreason: Confirmed in source. packages/core/src/styles.css:49 is unlayered (the only @layer in the file is `base` at :44), so `box-shadow: var(--brand-shadow)` beats the Tailwind v4 (4.3.3) `focus-visible:ring-[3px]` utility in @layer utilities, which is also a box-shadow. button.tsx:8 sets `outline-none`. The docs site masks this with globals.css `button:focus-visible{outline:3px solid var(--ring)}`, and that rule does not ship with core. Input still gets a border-colour change, so the defect is total for Button and partial for Input. Nothing in the docs makes this a deliberate decision; docs/apple-design-audit.md treats focus-visible as a requirement. I lowered it from P0 to P1: the reference site itself passes, and the failure only appears in a consumer that skips the docs globals. The fix (layer the rule, or add an outline-based focus) is correct and cheap.

surviving.title: All 35 pages share one identical meta description although per-page copy already exists in the code
surviving.evidence: Every route sampled (/, /brand, /tokens, /typography, /components, /navigation, /praesentation, /praesentationslogik, /icons, plus the 404) returns the same <meta name="description" content="Atlas, das Designsystem von Rapold: ein Designstandard mit austauschbaren Brands…">. surviving.fix: Move the descriptions map from reference-page.tsx into catalog.ts (keyed by page id, with guidance[id].intro as fallback). Return it as description, openGraph.description and twitter.description from the shared metadata helper in PERF-03. Add a test in tests/ that fails when two pages share a description.

This deviates from Google's guidance on unique descriptions, and the per-page copy already exists in the code. The fix is low-effort and has no downside.

surviving.title: Horizontal page scroll at 320px on /dashboard and /charts
surviving.evidence: At a 320px viewport (the 400% zoom equivalent), document scrollWidth is 341 against clientWidth 320. The offender is `Illustrative Daten, keine Projektkennzahlen` inside `.filter-bar` (data-showcase.tsx:9), 220px wide with its right edge at 341. CSS: globals.css:21 `.filter-bar{display:flex;gap:20px}` and `.filter-bar>span{white-space:nowrap}`. The other 33 routes reflow cleanly at 320 and 375.

surviving.fix: At ≤767px add `.filter-bar{flex-wrap:wrap}` and `.filter-bar>span{white-space:normal}`, or drop nowrap globally.

surviving.title: All overlay enter/exit motion is dead code: animate-in/fade/zoom/slide utilities are never generated
surviving.evidence:
dialog.tsx:35/63, sheet.tsx:34/60-68, popover.tsx:30, select.tsx:60, dropdown-menu.tsx:37/205 and tooltip.tsx:42 all use `animate-in fade-in-0 zoom-in-95 slide-in-from-*`.

No tw-animate-css or tailwindcss-animate exists in package.json or node_modules. The built CSS (_next/static/chunks/3bvtb48uz92n4.css, identical to live) contains only `.animate-pulse` and `.animate-spin`. No `.animate-in`, `.fade-in-0` or `.zoom-in-95` is generated.

Measured live: open Dialog shows animationName 'none' and animationDuration '0s', the overlay shows 'none', and select-content shows 'none'.

The declared durations are also off-token: sheet `duration-500`/`duration-300 ease-in-out`, dialog `duration-200`. The tokens are --duration-fast 150, normal 180 (rapold), slow 300 and deliberate 500, and --easing-enter/exit.
surviving.principle: Motion supports orientation (Atlas /accessibility & /motion copy); Material/Apple HIG: overlays need spatial continuity; design-token single source of truth
surviving.fix: Add `tw-animate-css` at an exact pinned version and `@import 'tw-animate-css'` in core styles.css. Alternatively, define enter/exit keyframes in core that read `var(--duration-normal)`, `var(--easing-enter)` and `var(--easing-exit)`. Replace the hard-coded duration-500/300/200 and ease-in-out with token-driven classes (e.g. `duration-(--duration-slow) ease-(--easing-exit)`). Then assert in a browser test that animationName != 'none' on dialog open (without reduced motion).
surviving.harm_chain: Consumers copy the classes believing motion is specified, nothing animates, each product invents its own motion, the motion tokens documented on /motion are never exercised
surviving.anticipated_refutation: 'Instant is fine and reduced-motion friendly.' Then the classes and the /motion promises should be removed. Today they document behavior that does not exist.
surviving.vreason: Confirmed. There is no tw-animate-css or tailwindcss-animate in node_modules and no @plugin/@import for one in globals.css or core styles.css. Nine `animate-in` usages exist across the core ui files. The live CSS on /components contains only `.animate-pulse` and `.animate-spin`. The enter/exit classes are dead code and the motion tokens go unused. Downgraded to P2: overlays still open and close correctly (instant is functional and reduced-motion friendly), so the core task is not blocked. This is a contract/consistency gap.

surviving.title: Buttons used as Radix triggers (asChild) lose brand sizing: 36px/14px vs 44px/16px
surviving.evidence:
styles.css:50 sizes buttons by `[data-slot="button"][data-size="default"]` (min-height 44px, font 1rem). Radix Slot merges the trigger's `data-slot` over the Button's.

Measured on /components?brand=rapold:
- plain buttons are 44px tall at 16px font,
- dialog-trigger 'Dialog öffnen' is 36px at 14px,
- sheet-trigger, dropdown-menu-trigger, popover-trigger and tooltip-trigger are all 36px at 14px.
The dark-mode screenshot (comp-d.png) shows the visibly smaller 'Dialog öffnen' next to the larger 'Erfolg' and 'Fehler'.

The same override hits box-shadow (VISUAL-01): trigger buttons get Tailwind shadow-xs while plain ones get brand-shadow.
surviving.principle: Consistency & standards (Nielsen #4); Apple HIG/WCAG 2.5.8 target size consistency; component API should not change visuals by composition
surviving.fix: Put brand sizing into the cva itself, e.g. `default: 'min-h-(--brand-button-height) px-5 text-base'`. Or key the CSS on `[data-variant][data-size]` (set by Button and not overwritten by Slot) instead of data-slot. Add a visual regression check comparing trigger and plain Button height.
surviving.vreason: Confirmed mechanism. Button (button.tsx:53-58) sets `data-slot="button"` and then spreads `{...props}` after it. When a Radix Trigger with asChild uses Slot to inject `data-slot="dialog-trigger"` etc., that prop overrides the button's data-slot. The brand rules in styles.css:49-50 keyed on `[data-slot="button"]` then no longer match, so sizing, font and shadow fall back to cva defaults (h-9/text-sm). The 36px vs 44px measurement is consistent with this. Real consistency defect, P2.

surviving.title: Form demo validation mixes native bubbles and custom errors: the custom error is unreachable and stale
surviving.evidence: pattern-showcase.tsx forms branch: the Input has `required minLength={3}` and no `noValidate` on the form. Live on /forms: entering 'ab' and submitting shows no custom error; the browser's English bubble appears instead ('Please lengthen this text to 3 characters or more…') on a de-CH page. The custom 'Der Projektname braucht mindestens drei Zeichen.' appears only for '   ' (three spaces). After the user types a valid value, aria-invalid stays 'true' and the error text persists until the next submit. The 'Ziel und Nutzen' textarea has only native `required` and no associated error. The component-demo form (component-demo.tsx:11) behaves the same way.
surviving.principle: WCAG 3.3.1 Error Identification, 3.3.3 Error Suggestion. Validation timing: validate on blur or submit and clear errors on correction (Wroblewski / NN/g inline validation).
surviving.fix: Add `noValidate` to the form and validate both fields in one function. On submit, set per-field errors and focus the first invalid field. Re-validate on change once a field has errored, so the error clears as soon as the value is valid. Set `aria-describedby` only when an error is present, and give the textarea its own error id. Optionally add an error summary for more than two fields. Ship this as a core `FormField` (Label, control, hint, error) so products cannot get the wiring wrong.
surviving.harm_chain: Teams copy a pattern whose documented custom error never shows and whose invalid state never clears.
surviving.anticipated_refutation: Native validation is acceptable. Mixing native and custom produces two languages and two styles, and leaves the demo's documented behaviour unreachable.
surviving.vreason: Confirmed at pattern-showcase.tsx:19: no noValidate together with required and minLength={3}. Native validation pre-empts the custom 'mindestens drei Zeichen' error for 'ab'. aria-describedby is always set, the error is never cleared on change, and the textarea has no error of its own. Real 3.3.1 and 3.3.3 weaknesses in a demo pattern.

surviving.title: The canonical login pattern omits autocomplete, name and input hints
surviving.evidence: pattern-showcase.tsx login-pattern: `<Input id="login-email" type="email" required placeholder="name@firma.ch"/>`. Live attribute check on /login-pattern: autocomplete=null, name='', inputMode='', spellcheck=null, autocapitalize=null. This is the reference pattern product teams (Rapold Auth, Cockpit) are told to copy.
surviving.principle: WCAG 1.3.5 Identify Input Purpose (AA). Baymard/NN/g: password managers and autofill depend on autocomplete and name.
surviving.fix: Model the complete field: `<Input id="login-email" name="email" type="email" autoComplete="username" (or "email") inputMode="email" autoCapitalize="none" spellCheck={false} enterKeyHint="send" aria-describedby="login-hint login-error" required/>`. Add a visible hint and an error element. Document these attributes in the pattern copy and in contracts/engineering.md.
surviving.harm_chain: Products copy the pattern, ship login forms that password managers and autofill cannot fill, and fail the 1.3.5 audit.
surviving.anticipated_refutation: It is only a 'Design-Vorschau'. Reference patterns are exactly what agents and teams copy verbatim.
surviving.vreason: Confirmed at pattern-showcase.tsx:21: the field is `<Input id="login-email" type="email" required …/>` with no name or autoComplete. WCAG 1.3.5 applies to an email field. surviving.title: Inter is downloaded twice per weight (latin plus latin-ext): about 96 KB wasted on every first visit
surviving.evidence: globals.css:5-14 imports @fontsource/inter latin-{300..700}.css AND latin-ext-{300..700}.css. In @fontsource/inter 5.3.0 these per-subset files have no unicode-range (grep -c unicode-range latin-400.css = 0; the built rule in 3bvtb48uz92n4.css is '@font-face{font-family:Inter;…font-weight:400;src:url(../media/inter-latin-400-normal…)}' with no range). Playwright document.fonts shows 'Inter 400,Inter 400,Inter 500,Inter 500,Inter 600,Inter 600,Inter 700,Inter 700' loaded on /. File sizes: latin about 24 KB each and latin-ext about 36 KB each, so about 240 KB of fonts on a 538 KB home transfer. latin-ext is a superset, so the 4 latin files (about 97 KB) are pure waste. The 300 weight is declared but never loaded.
surviving.principle: Web font best practice: one face per weight and style, subset with unicode-range, prefer a variable font. Fewer bytes on the critical path for FCP and LCP and less font-swap CLS.
surviving.fix: Replace the 10 imports with a single variable font: npm i @fontsource-variable/inter and use @import '@fontsource-variable/inter/wght.css'. That index CSS ships unicode-range-subsetted faces, and only latin is fetched for de-CH text (about 48 KB). Alternatively import only the index.css per weight (which has unicode-range) and drop 300. Add <link rel="preload" as="font" type="font/woff2" crossorigin> for the latin file used above the fold.
surviving.vreason: Confirmed, but the rationale is wrong. globals.css:5-14 imports both latin-* and latin-ext-* for 300-700, and grep finds 0 unicode-range in latin-400.css and latin-ext-400.css, so both faces are fetched for every weight used. However, latin-ext is NOT a superset of latin: Fontsource and Google subset latin-ext to Latin Extended ranges (U+0100+), while German umlauts sit in latin (U+00C0-00FF). The waste is therefore the latin-ext files (35,000 B each versus 23,664 B for latin-400), not the latin files. Dropping latin as suggested would break basic text. The comment at globals.css:2-4 shows a deliberate latin-only intent, so the double fetch is a bug, not a decision. Correct fix: the variable font or index CSS with unicode-range, keep latin, and remove the unused 300 weight.

surviving.title: No Content-Security-Policy, no frame-ancestors or X-Frame-Options, no Permissions-Policy; HSTS without includeSubDomains or preload
surviving.evidence: curl -I https://atlas.rapold.io/ returns only Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=63072000, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin (from vercel.json headers). The unsafe-inline is needed because the Next export inlines self.__next_f pushes; tighten later with hashes. Also add X-Frame-Options: DENY, Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=(), interest-cohort=(), and Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy: same-origin. Extend HSTS to max-age=63072000; includeSubDomains; preload only after confirming all *.rapold.io hosts are HTTPS-only. Ship CSP as Report-Only first and check /charts (ECharts from /vendor) and /mermaid.

Live headers carry HSTS max-age=63072000 (Vercel default) and Referrer-Policy, with no CSP, X-Frame-Options or Permissions-Policy, and vercel.json only sets nosniff and Referrer-Policy. The dangerouslySetInnerHTML input is the viewer's own editor input (self-XSS only). This is defence-in-depth hygiene, so P3. Report-Only CSP first is the right approach. HSTS preload should not be added without checking all *.rapold.io hosts.

surviving.evidence: curl -I https://atlas.rapold.io/tokens/ returns HTTP/1.1 200 OK; /tokens.html returns 308. The canonical tag mitigates this, but both URLs resolve.

surviving.title: Duplicated download and clipboard helpers; one copy revokes the blob URL before the download starts
surviving.evidence: pattern-showcase.tsx:8 `a.click();URL.revokeObjectURL(url);` (synchronous revoke) versus orgchart-editor.tsx:19 `a.click();setTimeout(()=>URL.revokeObjectURL(url),1000);`. The clipboard try/catch is reimplemented with different messages in reference-page.tsx:27, pattern-showcase.tsx:12, orgchart-editor.tsx:32, icon-gallery.tsx:11, mermaid-diagram.tsx:52, presentation-page.tsx:36 and rapold-showcase.tsx:66, each with different stale-message handling (only presentation-page and rapold-showcase guard against races).

surviving.title: Organigram editor: silent maxLength truncation, no limits shown, and destructive removal without undo
surviving.evidence: orgchart-editor.tsx:39-40 set maxLength 75, 45, 30, 36, 32 and 36 on the inputs with no hint, counter or aria-describedby, so typing past the limit is silently dropped. The 'Entfernen' button deletes the selected department immediately (`filter((_,i)=>i!==selected)`) with no confirmation or undo toast, although the sonner Toaster is mounted. The department `<option key={i}>` uses the index as key.
surviving.principle: WCAG 3.3.2 Labels or Instructions. Nielsen #3 user control and #5 error prevention.

surviving.title: Mixed forms of address and avoidable English labels

surviving.principle: Nielsen H2 and H4; Atlas' own content rule (catalog.ts 'identische Begriffe für identische Sachverhalte')
surviving.fix: Pick one address form in the /content page: du for UI microcopy, infinitive for instructions. Use German labels where idiomatic ('Benachrichtigungen', 'Diagramme', 'Mail-Vorlagen', 'Anmeldeablauf', 'Bewegung'), and keep code identifiers (variant names) in <code>.

surviving.title: Accessible names don't contain the visible label (identity link and search trigger)
surviving.evidence:
framework-shell.tsx:130: the identity link has `aria-label={`${brand.name} · Startseite`}`. For the neutral brand, brand.name is 'Framework', but the visible text is 'Atlas 0.7.1'. The measured accessible name is 'Framework · Startseite'.

surviving.principle: WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name, A. Speech-input users say what they see.
surviving.fix: Identity: use `aria-label={`Atlas · Startseite`}` for neutral, or drop the aria-label and add ` · Startseite` after the visible text. Search: drop the aria-label when expanded, since the visible 'Suchen' plus aria-haspopup is enough. In rail mode use 'Suchen'.
surviving.vreason: Confirmed in framework-shell.tsx. The identity link's aria-label is `${brand.name} · Startseite`, while the visible text is 'Atlas <version>', so for the neutral brand the visible 'Atlas' is missing from the name. The search trigger's aria-label 'Seiten durchsuchen' overrides the visible 'Suchen'. surviving.title: Mobile toolbar selects are clipped to 90px at 12px font

surviving.principle: WCAG 1.4.4 Resize Text / 1.4.10 Reflow (legibility); iOS input-zoom heuristic
surviving.fix: Use 16px font on mobile selects. Either move brand and mode into the mobile Sheet as full-width labelled selects, or show a short visible label ('Marke', 'Modus') with an icon.

surviving.title: Changelog and release history are only on GitHub; no on-site changelog route
surviving.evidence: /changelog and /CHANGELOG.md return 404. The only link is on /engineering (reference-page.tsx:47 → https://github.com/marcelrapold/mra-atlas/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md). /health-status links /build-info.json and GitHub Actions (pattern-showcase.tsx:24). surviving.fix: Copy CHANGELOG.md into public/contracts/changelog.md during the contracts build (scripts/build-contracts.mjs). Render it at /changelog as a catalog page under 'Betrieb', list it in /llms.txt, and show 'v0.7.1 · 12.10.2026 · Changelog' in the footer, read from build-info.

surviving.title: Search fields duplicate the clear affordance and over-announce
surviving.evidence:
table-showcase.tsx:44 has `` plus a custom X button, and Chromium and WebKit render their own cancel button as well, so there are two clear controls. On /tables two live regions update on every keystroke: `

{filtered} von 250 Bausteinen

surviving.title: Mermaid editor errors are raw English library messages not associated with the textarea

surviving.title: Organigramm previews are scroll containers that keyboard users can't reach at narrow widths
surviving.evidence:
axe scrollable-region-focusable (2 nodes) on /organigramm at 375: `.org-preview` scrollWidth 744 / clientWidth 282 and `.governance-preview` 564 / 282. Neither has tabIndex or focusable content (globals.css:235 sets min-width 720/540 on the SVG).

surviving.title: Brand switcher is labelled 'Theme' (English), and its option names don't match the rest of the UI

surviving.title: Landmark and structure nits: aside nested in main, skip link focusable under aria-hidden, pages without subheadings
surviving.evidence:

surviving.title: Small or variable hit targets in core controls

surviving.title: Physical CSS properties instead of logical ones in the shell and core
surviving.evidence: globals.css: `.notice{border-left:3px solid var(--primary)}`, margin-left ×6, margin-right ×5, padding-left ×3, left: ×3, `text-align:left` (token-card, token-table, table). surviving.title: Ad-hoc Markdown renderer for a binding contract page
surviving.evidence:
praesentationslogik/page.tsx:15-16 splits docs/presentation-logic.md on '\n\n' and maps '## ' to h2, '- ' to ul and `/^\d\. /` to ol, with everything else as plain

surviving.title: Dead or orphaned code in the shell context and the CSS hacks

surviving.title: Third-party draft brand (Dominicano Express) is publicly indexable and shipped in the core JS of every page

If it is cleared, record the approval in the brand's provenance file.

surviving.title: Minified source CSS and TSX with duplicate and overriding rules, and no formatter
surviving.evidence: globals.css is 35,474 bytes on 51 lines. Line 21 is 13,761 characters, line 26 5,360, line 37 2,523. TSX lines reach 2,309 characters (icon-gallery.tsx) and 2,117 (reference-page.tsx, 12 lines over 200). There is no .prettierrc or .editorconfig. Duplicates and overrides: `.download-row a` styled on line 21 and again on line 26; `.doc-section>p` font-size 15px (line 21), then 16px (line 30); `.rail .nav-link` twice (lines 21 and 30); `.breadcrumb` redefined in globals lines 21, 31 and accessibility.css:3; the prefers-reduced-motion block duplicated in core styles.css and globals.css:24. 5 `!important` in globals (reduced motion ×3, plus `.type-row>span{font-size:min(7vw,36px)!important}` and `.deck-type-scale span{font-size:22px!important}`, both fighting inline styles).

Split globals.css into layered partials (shell.css, doc.css, deck.css, tables.css, mermaid.css) imported into `@layer components`. surviving.title: Brand-specific branching is spread across docs app files, contrary to the defineBrand/registry contract
surviving.evidence: framework-shell.tsx:104 `brand.id === 'rapold' ? {'--font-mono': '"Geist Mono"…'}`. brand-showcase.tsx:9 `if(brand.id==='rapold')return <RapoldShowcase/>`. catalog.ts:31,36 guidance per brandId. presentation-page.tsx:14-20 FAQ map keyed 'dominicano-express' and 'rapold'. changelog-infographic.tsx:81 `brand.id==='dominicano-express'?dominicanoChangelog:…`. rapold-worlds.tsx:13 `pulseColors={brand:'#0072ce',…}` duplicates brands/rapold/worlds.json:82. globals.css:16-18 imports brands/rapold/theme.css, wordmarks.css and worlds.css (about 600 lines) for every brand, including neutral. AGENTS.md: 'Neue Brands über defineBrand und Registry hinzufügen.'
surviving.principle: Open/closed principle. The repo's own contract (AGENTS.md, docs/brand-contract.md).

Import pulse colours from worlds.json rather than copying the hex values.

surviving.title: Semantic color roles collapse or drift: info == primary everywhere; Rapold danger/warning change hue family between modes
surviving.evidence:
In all 6 brand-modes --info equals --primary:
- rapold #0066B3 / #38B8FF
- neutral #263b70 / #adc4ff
- dominicano #146FE8 / #69ADFF

Rapold destructive is light #814960 (desaturated plum) vs dark #FB7185 (rose). Warning is light #816F31 (olive) vs dark #FBBF24 (amber).

The aria-invalid ring `ring-destructive/20` blends to 1.30–1.54:1 against the background.

By contrast, radiox statusTone.ts pins 'info→cyan, progress→sky, active→violet, error→rose' as distinct roles.
surviving.principle: Color carries a role (Atlas /dataviz copy: 'Farbe trägt eine Rolle'); WCAG 1.4.1 Use of Color; recognition over recall across modes
surviving.fix: Give info its own hue distinct from primary in every brand. Keep danger in the red family in both Rapold modes (e.g. light ~#B42339 at >=4.5:1 on #F4FAFF) and warning in the amber family. Import radiox's statusTone role set (success/info/progress/warning/error/neutral/active) into brand.schema.json as required roles with surface tints (the surface-info, surface-success etc. tokens already exist).
surviving.vreason: Confirmed: --info equals --primary in all published token files (e.g. rapold dark both #38B8FF; neutral light both #263b70). rapold.json:34/61 has destructive #814960 in light vs #FB7185 in dark, and warning #816F31 vs #FBBF24. The light values look like deliberate contrast-driven darkening rather than a random hue change, and info==primary may be an intentional simplification. Neither is documented as a decision, but no WCAG failure is demonstrated beyond the ring/20 halo already covered by VISUAL-01/05. Downgraded to P3 (semantic polish, worth aligning with radiox statusTone).

surviving.title: Collapsed rail: nav labels are only available as hover tooltips (title)
surviving.evidence:
framework-shell.tsx:111 renders rail group names as `<div className="rail-group" title={group.title}>` with sr-only text. framework-shell.tsx:117 gives rail links `title={rail ? title : undefined}` plus aria-label. Native title tooltips appear only on mouse hover, never on keyboard focus or touch.

Measured rail links are 47x36 icon-only (e.g. 'Marken & Identität'). A sighted keyboard user tabbing through 35 icons sees no label.
surviving.principle: WCAG 1.4.13 Content on Hover or Focus (intent), 2.4.6 Headings and Labels; Nielsen: recognition rather than recall. The info is hover-only.
surviving.fix: Wrap rail links and group markers in the core Tooltip (Radix shows on focus, dismisses on Escape, stays when hovered) with side='right', and remove `title`. Optionally widen the rail on focus-within.
surviving.vreason: Confirmed: rail links use `title` plus `aria-label`, and the group marker uses `title` plus sr-only text, so assistive tech gets the names. The WCAG citation is wrong: 1.4.13 governs extra content shown on hover or focus, not missing tooltips, and icon-only controls with accessible names pass 2.4.6 and 4.1.2. What remains is a usability point (recognition rather than recall for sighted keyboard users of the collapsed rail), which is optional. P3 with effort M.

surviving.title: Contract logic is untyped JS with hand-written declarations, and the strictness gaps hide index errors
surviving.evidence: tsconfig.json include covers only `**/*.ts, **/*.tsx`. There is no allowJs or checkJs, so packages/brands/src/*.mjs (orgchart 21.8 KB, deck-validation, index 7.8 KB, presentation) and packages/presentation/src/*.mjs are never type-checked. Six hand-maintained .d.ts/.d.mts files describe them and can drift (e.g. CODE-12 `format:string`; orgchart.d.mts `renderZustaendigkeiten(data:object…)`). `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` is off, hiding cases like orgchart-editor.tsx:24 `data.departments[selected]` (undefined after a delete race) and data-showcase.tsx:7 `brand.modes[mode]!` (non-null assertion). `tsc --noEmit` passes with 0 any or ts-ignore.

surviving.fix: Enable `allowJs` and `checkJs` for packages/** with JSDoc types, or convert the .mjs files to .ts and emit .d.ts. Turn on `noUncheckedIndexedAccess` and `exactOptionalPropertyTypes` and fix the fallout. Generate types for brand.schema.json and deck-input.schema.json (json-schema-to-typescript) instead of writing them by hand.
surviving.vreason: Confirmed: the tsconfig.json include covers only .ts and .tsx, with no allowJs, checkJs or noUncheckedIndexedAccess. The contract .mjs files are not type-checked, and the hand-written .d.mts files can drift. No concrete user-facing failure is shown, so P3.

surviving.title: Two chart libraries, a vendored 1.1 MB ECharts in git, and minor dependency lag
surviving.evidence: apps/docs/public/vendor/echarts-6.0.0.min.js (1,117,939 bytes, git-tracked) is loaded with next/script in echarts-showcase.tsx:50, while recharts ^3.10.1 is also a dependency (data-showcase, reference-page charts tabs). `npm outdated`: next 16.3.5→16.4.0, radix-ui 1.6.7→1.8.0, lucide-react 1.45→1.55, react/react-dom 19.2.7→19.3.0, mermaid 12.0→12.1, tailwind-merge 3.6→3.7, @tanstack/react-table 8.21.3→9.2.8 (major). Decide whether Atlas recommends one chart library or both, and document why. Add Renovate grouped weekly with exact pins. Drive the icon gallery from /icons/index.json and lazy SVGs.

surviving.title: The docs app does not use the core Select: about 12 raw selects, styled by a global rule, with mixed labelling

surviving.title: Rapold brand page is 9.5k px (12.9k mobile); the download path is buried behind the marketing 'Produktwelten'

surviving.title: Elevation is not tokenized and ignores brand/mode
surviving.evidence:
Brand shadows are rapold 'none', neutral 'none' and dominicano '0 1px 3px #00000014' in both light and dark. The Dialog still renders Tailwind shadow-lg ('0 10px 15px -3px rgba(0,0,0,.1)…', measured in all 6 brand-modes). surviving.title: Docs site ignores its own spacing/type/z-index tokens; heavy off-scale values
surviving.evidence:
In apps/docs/app/globals.css (520 rules) the token references are:
- var(--spacing-*): 0
- var(--font-size-*): 0
- var(--line-height-*): 0
- var(--z-index-*): 0
- var(--layout-reading): 0

Spacing values that are off the 4px scale (4/8/12/16/20/24/32…): 10px x27, 18px x21, 14px x14, 6px x12, 28px x12, 9px x9, 22px x9, 7px x7, 5px x7, 3px x5, 30px x5, plus 26, 34, 35, 38 and 42px. That is about 150 of about 420 declarations.

Font sizes: 13px x27, 11px x11, 10px x2, 15px x8, plus 22, 25, 27 and 29px. The scale is 12/14/16/18/20/24/30/36/48(56).

Line-heights: 13 distinct values against 4 tokens.

z-index: 1, 10, 20 and 100, against tokens 20/30/40/50/60/70. Core primitives also hard-code z-50 for tooltip, select and dropdown, while the tokens say tooltip 70 and dropdown 30.
surviving.principle: Design-token single source of truth (Atlas /engineering: 'Eine Quelle pro Entscheidung'); Gestalt rhythm; 8-pt grid consistency
surviving.fix: Refactor globals.css to `var(--spacing-N)`, `var(--font-size-*)` and `var(--line-height-*)`. Snap off-scale values to the nearest step and raise 10–11px labels to 12px (font-size-xs). Map z-index utilities to tokens via @theme (`--z-tooltip: var(--z-index-tooltip)`). Add a stylelint rule that rejects raw px in spacing and font-size properties in apps/docs.
surviving.vreason: Confirmed: globals.css has 0 occurrences each of var(--spacing-*) and var(--font-size-*), and core hard-codes z-50 in dialog, dropdown, popover, select, sheet, tooltip and lightbox. However, globals.css is the docs site's own chrome, not the consumable contract, and an effort-L refactor of about 150 declarations has low user impact. The z-index token mismatch in core is the only consumer-relevant part. Downgraded to P3.

surviving.title: No i18n layer: all copy is inlined, core defaults are a mix of English and German, slugs and labels mix languages
surviving.evidence: There is no messages module, t() or locale context anywhere in apps/docs or packages/core. All copy is inline JSX across 20 components, including whole paragraphs in reference-page.tsx (13 inline descriptions in a `descriptions` object at line 24) and catalog.ts. Core defaults: 'Close' (dialog, sheet, command) versus German-only lightbox strings. On the de-CH page, English UI labels: framework-shell.tsx:143 `<label …>Theme</label>`, :144 option 'Default', :159 `aria-label="Mobile Navigation"`. Route slugs mix languages: /forms, /tables, /charts, /components alongside /organigramm, /praesentation, /formulare→404. The mail template uses `<html lang="de">` (pattern-showcase.tsx:22) while the site is de-CH. radiox already has the resolution chain Atlas lacks: apps/frontend/services/locale.ts (user locale, then navigator.language, then 'de-CH', with SUPPORTED_LOCALES).
surviving.principle: i18n readiness: externalised strings and locale-aware formatting. WCAG 3.1.1/3.1.2 (language of page and parts).
surviving.fix: Introduce `apps/docs/app/_i18n/de-CH.ts` (typed message object) and import strings from it, starting with the shell, forms and patterns. For core, standardise a `labels` prop or a `<CoreLocaleProvider labels={…}>` with English defaults, and supply de-CH from the docs app. Import radiox's `services/locale.ts` pattern into @rapold/framework-core as `resolveLocale()`. Label the selector 'Brand' consistently in German (e.g. 'Marke'). Decide the slug language and add redirects for the other variant. Emit `lang="de-CH"` in the mail template.
surviving.harm_chain: Rapold products with English or French audiences cannot reuse core components without forking, and machine translation of the site is impossible without touching every component.
surviving.anticipated_refutation: Atlas is de-CH only. The core is explicitly white-label and consumed by multiple products. The docs app can stay German, but the core cannot hardcode German.
surviving.vreason: English strings on the de-CH site are confirmed (framework-shell.tsx:143 'Theme', :159 'Mobile Navigation'), and there is no i18n layer. Atlas is documented as German-Swiss (README.md:17), so a full i18n layer is speculative for the docs app. The core-locale part overlaps CODE-09. P3.

surviving.title: Initial JS of about 267 KB br / 823 KB raw on mostly static documentation pages; the whole shell and all page content are client components
surviving.evidence: Home page scripts (brotli/raw bytes, measured): 26swit4g4lpuz.js 72,696/228,084 (react-dom), 2s4mrsztopiw2.js 46,638/172,201, 0wymy5fz8r9ns.js 23,282/62,195 (contains presentationTheme, compilePrompt, echarts/mermaid references), 0kh83j3ewd-mm.js 18,640/47,950 (cmdk, all brand registries incl. 'Dominicano Express'), 44r8hm6_kwaka.js, 14ygvkdw6jsfl.js, 136-qpyufe0np.js and others. That totals about 267 KB br excluding the noModule polyfill. CSS 3bvtb48uz92n4.css is 26,853 br / 136,756 raw and render-blocking. framework-shell.tsx and reference-page.tsx are both 'use client'. reference-page.tsx statically imports presentation.mjs, prompt-compiler.mjs and contrast utils, plus the whole catalog guidance text (catalog.ts, 12 KB) for every route.
surviving.principle: web.dev JS budget guidance (keep the critical-path JS small; TBT and INP scale with parse and execute work on mid-range mobile). Next.js RSC best practice: keep static content in Server Components.
surviving.fix: Make ReferencePage a Server Component that renders guidance, headings and tables from catalog.ts on the server, and keep only interactive islands (search dialog, brand/mode switch, copy buttons, demos) as client components. Lazy-import presentation.mjs and prompt-compiler.mjs only in the sections that use them (praesentation, prompt-compiler). Load brand registries per brand (dynamic import by id) instead of bundling all three. Track this with a bundle budget in scripts/check-build.mjs, e.g. fail if first-load JS for / exceeds 180 KB br.
surviving.vreason: Partly verified. framework-shell.tsx and reference-page.tsx are both 'use client', so all page content ships as client JS. I did not re-measure the per-chunk byte figures. For a developer and agent reference site visited on desktop, about 267 KB br is a best-practice deviation without demonstrated user harm (no INP or TBT data). The L-effort RSC refactor is disproportionate compared with PERF-02 and PERF-05, which partly overlap. A bundle budget in check-build is a reasonable low-cost step, so P3.

surviving.title: Whole app is client-side, with god components switching over 18 or more sections
surviving.evidence: layout.tsx:15 wraps all children in the 'use client' FrameworkShell. reference-page.tsx is a single 'use client' component branching on 18 section ids (`section==='tokens'`, 'brand' ×2, 'mermaid' ×2, …). It imports presentation.mjs, prompt-compiler.mjs, resolveFoundation and the whole catalog for every route, and holds unrelated state (query, repo, motionKey, selected). pattern-showcase.tsx:10 holds 9 useState hooks for 11 unrelated sections. /brand loads 14 script chunks, the largest 72.7 KB compressed. Static explanatory copy that could ship as server-rendered HTML is hydrated.
surviving.principle: React Server Components boundary: keep static content on the server and hydrate only interactive islands. Single responsibility.
surviving.fix: Turn each section into its own server component file (`sections/tokens.tsx`, …) chosen by a map in [section]/page.tsx. Mark only interactive parts 'use client' (token copy buttons, prompt builder, editors). Give the shell a server layout plus a small client 'BrandControls' island (combine with CODE-04). Split PatternShowcase into one component per pattern.
surviving.vreason: layout.tsx:15 wraps everything in the client FrameworkShell. With a static export, client components are still prerendered to HTML, so content stays crawlable. The cost is bundle size and hydration, and no CWV failure was shown. The architectural refactor is valid but low impact: P3.

scores.why: Strong system status (aria-current, copy status, asset load/retry) and good dialog focus handling. Consistency (H4=4) and recognition (H6=4) are dragged down by the naming chaos, signets hidden behind the brand switch and title-only search.
Clean visual hierarchy and no dark patterns. But 35 expanded nav items, duplicate pages and prompt builders, a 9.5k px brand page, 30 px mobile targets and a prefilled repo field.

Precise, factual German with Swiss spelling (no ß) and honest demo notices. But the hero has no value proposition, there are six names for the neutral brand, a mislabeled 'Vertrag als JSON', an English 404, mixed address forms and the 4-vs-10 signets mismatch.
Tokens, icons and decks work in 2–3 actions. Signets need hidden knowledge, components have no usage code, the integration guide is unlinked and the spacing name is wrong.
Taxonomy mixes audience and artefact type; there are duplicate labels; search only indexes page titles (0 hits for Signet/Button/Farbe/Deck); 3 of the 10 key intents fail or need prior knowledge.

Polished Rapold brand page and a calm shell. But H1 'Übersicht', three different Atlas marks, a generic OG image dropped on 32 pages, no manifest/apple-touch/theme-color despite Atlas' own checklist, and the default English 404.

Every route has exactly one h1 and labelled navs, plus main and footer. Problems: EmptyState forces an h1→h3 skip, an aside is nested in main, 8 routes have no subheadings, and the breadcrumb is not a nav.

scores.dimension: Keyboard operability (palette, dialogs, sheets, tabs, selects, rail)
scores.why: Everything tested is operable. Focus traps and focus return are correct on the palette, Sheet, Dialog, deck dialog and Lightbox, and Escape works everywhere. Problems: the organigramm scroll regions are not focusable, and the rail labels are hover-only.

The Atlas shell shows a strong 3px outline. But the core Button/Input focus ring is overridden (P0 for consumers), Input focus is a 1px border change that vanishes in forced colors, and SC 2.4.11 fails on /praesentation, /mermaid and mobile /components.

Names are generally good and aria-activedescendant works. Problems: 2.5.3 mismatches on the identity link and search trigger, an aria-label on a role-less div, 'Theme' vs 'Marke' naming, and the skip link stays tabbable under aria-hidden.

scores.dimension: Contrast across light/dark and each brand
scores.why: Dark mode has 0 failures across 3 brands × 35 routes. Light mode: the Tabs primitive fails in all brands (3.85–4.39), Dominicano primary-as-text fails site-wide at 4.2, and the eyebrow opacity fails in rapold and dominicano.
No 2.5.8 failures; undersized targets are isolated. Against 44px on touch: tabs 29px, checkbox 16px, inputs 36px, sort and footer links 18–19px. The pointer:coarse coverage is partial.
Global CSS reset in both core and docs; ECharts, Recharts and the Rapold worlds respect it, and the worlds also have pause and forced-colors states.
33/35 routes reflow at 320. /dashboard and /charts overflow by 21px. The text-spacing override caused no clipping except intentional line-clamps.

No overflow from 375 to 1920. Tables use labelled scroll regions and filmstrips are labelled. Problems: the sticky stack hides focus, rail labels are hover-only, mobile toolbar selects are clipped to 90px/12px, and the 1024 touch case relies on pointer:coarse.
Unique titles, and the Next route announcer reads the title. Palette and mobile navigation focus main. Desktop sidebar navigation leaves focus on the link, which is acceptable with the announcer.
Clear sidebar/header/content shell and a strong h1. But body copy is muted, the h2/body step is weak, there is no h3, and the home card grid gives every destination equal weight.
A 4px token scale exists, but the docs use 0 spacing tokens and about 150 off-scale px values.
Good font loading and a defined scale. But 13, 11 and 10px sizes sit off-scale, there are 13 line-heights, and prose runs 96–105 characters per line.
Every role pair passes contrast (>=4.45:1). But info equals primary, Rapold danger and warning drift hue between modes, and there is no progress, neutral or active role.
All 3 brands have complete dark palettes with good contrast. Points lost to the neutral/light flash before hydration and shadows that are invisible in dark mode.
A single Lucide set, a stroke token and consistent size-4 defaults. Brand signets are kept separate.
Published radius tokens differ from the rendered values, buttons and dialogs use mixed radii, and elevation is not tokenized.
Missing: loading, active, indeterminate, field error, Textarea, status badges, Switch/Progress/Alert. Focus rings are overridden on Button and Input.
Local actions give instant toasts and role=status messages. But there is no loading affordance, and the promise demo resolves instantly.
Good tokens exist, but no overlay animation is ever generated, and the declared classes use non-token durations.
Global resets exist in core and docs and were verified live. They lack a non-motion loading cue and give no feedback on /motion.
There is no confirm or AlertDialog primitive, the demo delete does nothing, the destructive menu variant is undocumented and the hover is weak.
The form error path is unreachable and the loading toast is never seen. There is no hover/focus/disabled/invalid gallery and no light/dark comparison.

Good static delivery: TTFB about 55 ms, FCP/LCP about 1.5 s on throttled /, /tokens and /praesentation; heavy libraries lazy; immutable hashed chunks. Lost points: CLS 0.165 and 0.118 on /icons and /components, LCP 3.8 s on /icons, about 267 KB br initial JS because everything is a client component, Inter downloaded twice per weight (about 96 KB wasted), a light-theme flash for dark users, and max-age=0 on versioned vendor and font assets.

robots, sitemap (matches all 35 exported pages), self-canonicals, unique titles, one H1, lang=de-CH and llms.txt are in place. But descriptions are identical sitewide, og:image and og:locale are missing on 32 section pages, twitter:title is 'Atlas' everywhere, brand variants and interactive references are JS-only (Rapold signets are invisible to curl/WebFetch), the 404 canonicalises to /, and there is no JSON-LD or lastmod.

HTTPS plus 2-year HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, a real 404 status, no cookies or trackers, mermaid securityLevel strict, a sandboxed mail iframe, a visible version and a build-info.json commit that matches HEAD. Missing: CSP, frame-ancestors/XFO and Permissions-Policy; no imprint or privacy notice; changelog only off-site on GitHub; a draft third-party brand publicly indexed.

Core is genuinely brand-free with a clean portal contract. However, the docs app is fully client-side, has god components, uses deep imports into brands/src, and spreads brand-id branches across files. Brand and mode are resolved only after hydration, so static HTML is always neutral.

Mermaid, ECharts and the asset manifest fetch handle cancellation and fallbacks well, and copy races are guarded in places. On the other side, the organigram editor's derived state destroys input, validation state goes stale, clipboard and download helpers are duplicated, and one revokes the blob URL synchronously.

Zero hex values in core. The orgchart palette and the #16181d and #fff fallbacks sit outside the tokens, Rapold hex and CSS are hardwired in the docs, and the mono font override is not part of the brand contract.

Unlayered core and docs CSS overrides Tailwind utilities (the measured Input focus ring is gone and the dialog title renders at 20px instead of 18px). Lines run to 13.7k characters, selectors are duplicated, and !important is used against inline styles.

strict passes with no any. However, the .mjs contract logic is unchecked and its declarations are hand-written, there is no noUncheckedIndexedAccess, no lint, and no component, e2e or a11y tests, so three confirmed UI bugs pass CI.
Mostly current with exact pins for the core stack. A 1.1 MB ECharts file is vendored in git next to Recharts, there is a pending TanStack v9 major, and pinning is mixed.

scores.dimension: Forms (labels, autocomplete, inputmode, validation timing, error association)
scores.why: Labels are mostly present and status regions are used. The login pattern lacks autocomplete and input hints (WCAG 1.3.5), validation mixes native English bubbles with unreachable custom errors, the editor swallows newlines, and limits are silent.

scores.dimension: i18n readiness (strings, Intl, lang, logical CSS, expansion)
scores.why: lang=de-CH is correct and layout tolerates +35% text expansion. There is no string externalisation, core defaults mix English and German, there are three number conventions and only one Intl call, display labels double as logic keys, and the CSS uses physical properties.

protect.p: Rapold signet matrix and download system (apps/docs/app/_components/rapold-showcase.tsx): a one-click SVG download per product × variant with descriptive aria-labels, a ZIP per product, an asset table driven by the asset manifest with explicit loading, error and retry states, and the usage snippet that explains alt text. Make it easier to find; do not redesign it.

The deck flow on /praesentation (presentation-page.tsx and packages/brands/src/prompt-compiler.mjs): repository and Anlass go into a deterministic short prompt that points at /brands/{id}/management.md. One copy button with a fallback message. The gallery is rendered from the real PPTX (with a hash gate), and the slide dialog explains zones and the typical mistake for each slide. This is the strongest journey on the site.

Brand context through ?brand= plus localStorage persistence, together with machine-readable contracts per brand (/brands/{id}/llms.txt, tokens.{mode}.json|css|dtcg.json, brand.json) and the click-to-copy var(--role) token cards. Keep the URLs and the file names stable. Also keep the precise, Swiss-spelled German writing principles (no ß, «» quotes, no invented numbers).

Shell focus management in apps/docs/app/_components/framework-shell.tsx:126-167. The skip link targets <main id=main tabIndex=-1>. The command palette's onCloseAutoFocus returns focus to the element that opened it, or to <main> after navigating. The mobile Sheet hands focus to <main> after a link and to the palette after search. Measured: Escape returns focus to the trigger every time, and palette navigation lands on MAIN with the Next route announcer reading the page title. Pages have unique titles such as 'Typografie · Atlas'.

Motion and input-modality handling. There is a global prefers-reduced-motion reset in core styles.css:53-55 and globals.css. At the JS level: ECharts animation follows matchMedia (echarts-showcase.tsx), Recharts 3.10 uses isAnimationActive='auto', the Rapold product-worlds have pause, reduced-motion and forced-colors states (worlds.css:194,281,287), and the lightbox hint shows on focus and under hover:none. The pointer:coarse 44px block in accessibility.css:15-18 also stays. Do not replace any of these with hover-only or animation-only cues.

Accessible data alternatives and structure. Every chart has role=img, a summary aria-label and a real <table> with caption. The data table is a focusable, labelled scroll region with aria-sort (table-showcase.tsx:45-48). Every route has exactly one h1. Dark mode passed axe contrast with 0 failures on all 35 routes in all three brands.

Contrast-validated semantic role tokens per brand and mode: all 19 text/fill role pairs measure >=4.45:1 (most 5-17:1) in all 6 brand-modes. Examples: rapold-light primary-foreground/primary 5.91:1, muted-foreground/background 6.10:1. Keep the generator and the 'npm run check' contrast gate that produce public/brands/*/tokens.*.css.

The global prefers-reduced-motion reset in packages/core/src/styles.css:53 and in apps/docs/app/globals.css. It was verified live: under reduce, the motion-sample and skeleton animation durations compute to 1e-05s. Keep it scoped so brand portals (useBrandPortal) inherit it.

One icon language: Lucide everywhere, a single stroke token (svg.lucide{stroke-width:var(--icon-stroke,1.5)}), size-4 defaults in Button, Sonner and menus, and a 44px --brand-button-height on plain Buttons. Plus the Radix primitives that already give Escape, focus trap and focus return in Dialog, Sheet and Popover.

Fully static export behind Vercel's CDN, with immutable hashed /_next/static assets, a real HTTP 404 status (noindex) for missing pages, HTTPS with HSTS and an http to https 308. Measured TTFB is ~55 ms and FCP/LCP is ~1.5 s on /, /tokens and /praesentation under 4x CPU and slow-network throttling. Do not move to SSR or functions for content that is static.

The agent-contract surface: /llms.txt, /brands/index.json, /brands/{brand}/llms.txt, /contracts/*.md, token exports, /icons/{Name}.svg and /build-info.json, whose commit fd6bd84 matches repo HEAD. The visible version (Atlas 0.7.1 in the sidebar) plus a dated CHANGELOG are strong permanence and provenance signals for the primary audience (agents).

Heavy libraries are lazy and kept off the main bundle: mermaid (1.47 MB raw), cytoscape, katex, recharts and ECharts all load through next/dynamic, Radix TabsContent or next/script only on their own route or tab. Mermaid runs with securityLevel:'strict' (mermaid-diagram.tsx:35, mermaid-showcase.tsx:35) and the mail preview iframe is sandbox="". Keep this lazy, sandboxed setup.

Core stays brand-free: grep for hex, rgb() or oklch(), 'Rapold', 'Geist' and brand names across packages/core/src returns zero hits. BrandProvider (packages/core/src/brand-provider.tsx:11-16) gives Dialog, Select, Popover and DropdownMenu a portal container inside the brand scope (useBrandPortal), so overlays inherit the brand variables. Keep this contract and its AGENTS.md rule.

Async error and loading discipline in the heavy renderers. mermaid-diagram.tsx:22-47 combines a cancellation flag, a serialised renderQueue, a 30,000-character limit, securityLevel 'strict' and a readable error fallback. rapold-showcase.tsx:52-58 uses an AbortController with a retry state. The ECharts showcase falls back to a data table when the library fails. Keep these patterns when refactoring.

Text-expansion resilience and de-CH consistency. Pseudo-localised text at +35% (breakable words) at 375px caused zero overflow and zero ellipsis clipping on /, /components, /tables, /praesentation, /tokens and /forms. The site uses lang="de-CH", og:locale de_CH, Swiss 'ss' spelling and «» quotes throughout, and `npm run check` (contract tests, typecheck and build) runs in CI on every push.
